conviction_note: Consensus core EPS ($1.31, Zacks and Benzinga agree) sits almost exactly on the midpoint of the company's own H2 2026 guide (NIM 4.25-4.35% on $6.85-6.95B earning assets, fees $18-22M, expense $94-98M per half). The newest information is a 25bp Fed hike on 2026-09-16 into a balance sheet management calls 'positioned to do well' in rising rates, which helps the Q4 guide, against a peer (FB Financial, 2026-10-13) showing deposit costs up and NIM down 12bp. The findings net to about zero, the name's reactions are small (median 1.76%, last beat +0.47%), so p_up 52 on abs 2.5 gives +0.1; the findings sum (+0.05) and the scaled number agree.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $1.31 (Zacks via briefglance 2026-10-02, https://briefglance.com/articles/equity-bancshares-q3-preview-ma-strategy-meets-market-momentum ; Benzinga Q3'26E $1.31, revenue ~$85.0M, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EQBK/earnings-forecasts). Earnings Whispers $1.32, TickFlow $1.27 (3 analysts, $1.23-$1.31). Two sources agree at $1.31, so the bar is sourced. Company guide (H2 2026, from the Q2 release 2026-07-14 https://investor.wedbush.com/wedbush/article/bizwire-2026-7-14-equity-bancshares-inc-second-quarter-results-highlighted-by-strong-earnings-momentum-and-margin-expansion and Quartr call summary https://quartr.com/events/equity-bancshares-inc-eqbk-q2-2026_ozHJHmID): NIM 4.25-4.35% leaning high end, avg earning assets $6.85-6.95B, non-interest income $18-22M, non-interest expense $94-98M for the half. My arithmetic on the guide midpoints: NII ~$74M/q + fees ~$10M - expense ~$48M - provision ~$2M, 21.5% tax, ~20.4M diluted shares = ~$1.31. The consensus is the guide midpoint; the print lands inside the guide unless rates or credit moved. Last quarter core EPS $1.41 vs $1.24 consensus (GAAP $1.27); four straight EPS beats per Benzinga, but Q2 revenue $81.9M missed $84.9M.
positioning_check: Short interest 591,717 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 2.87% of 20.59M shares outstanding, 5.48 days to cover, up from 441,012 (2.14%, 3.25 days) at 2026-07-31; highest of the last six settlements and rising two in a row (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/eqbk/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). Not crowded. Options unusable: front-expiry chain has 288 total OI, ATM spread 186% of mid, no skew number (baseline). Put/call OI ratio 0.06 on tiny OI, meaningless. Run-up -5.0% over 20 days, -0.53% over 5 days, 9.6% below the 52-week high; spot $46.75 (intraday, 2026-10-14 15:59 UTC) is about 6% below the $49.85 at which the Lincoln deal was struck on 2026-09-02, near the $45.02 average buyback price of Q2. Realised vol 12.8% annualised, very quiet.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), the first move since a hold at 3.50-3.75% that ran from Dec 2025 to July 2026; on the Q2 call CFO Navratil said the balance sheet's positioning has not meaningfully changed since the last rising-rate cycle and the company is 'positioned to do well' in it, while guiding H2 NIM 4.25-4.35% (modestly lower than Q2's 4.36%) on accretion burn-down and mix, a guide set before any hike. Only two weeks of the hike fall in Q3, so the effect lands on the Q4 NIM guide and the call commentary on 2026-10-15, where a hold-or-raise of the NIM range against a 'modestly lower' guide is the upside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (NIM +3bp to 4.36%, core EPS $1.41 vs $1.24, guide NIM modestly lower): stock +0.47% (baseline). Q2 2025 -6.63% is the largest reaction in the history; cause not established here. Margin news has not produced large moves in the 7 sealed prints (median |move| 1.76%).
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, but the company's H2 NIM guide predates it and sell-side consensus ($1.31) still sits on the guide midpoint, so the EPS bar has not been moved for the rate change. If the market had priced a NIM upgrade, consensus would sit above the guide midpoint and the stock would not be 5% down over 20 days and 6% below the deal-announcement price.
findings.independence: Management's rate-sensitivity comment is from the Q2 call as summarised by MarketBeat (snippet_only, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/equity-bancshares-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-15/, 2026-07-15); the guide is from the Quartr summary https://quartr.com/events/equity-bancshares-inc-eqbk-q2-2026_ozHJHmID. The peer finding below (FB Financial deposit costs up) cuts against the transmission, and that is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: FB Financial (FBK), a southeastern regional that reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-13 after EQBK last spoke, posted NIM down 12bp to 3.83% from 3.95% with interest-bearing deposit costs up to 2.88% from 2.81% and total deposit cost up to 2.32% from 2.26%, attributed to 'increased pricing on interest-bearing deposits' (funding costs rising faster than asset yields, asset yield down 5bp). That is the first calendar-Q3 2026 US regional print found and a negative read for deposit pricing into a hiking cycle; EQBK's brokered deposits had already risen to 8.0% of deposits from 5.7% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EQBK Q2 2026 NIM +3bp: +0.47%. No sourced EQBK reaction to a NIM miss in the sealed history.
findings.why_not_priced: Released yesterday on a different bank in a different region; EQBK consensus was set before it (Zacks $1.31 as of 2026-10-02) and EQBK trades about $5M a day with thin coverage, so a peer read-through is unlikely to have reached the EQBK estimate. If it had, consensus would sit below the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: Proxy only: different footprint (Tennessee vs Kansas/Oklahoma/Missouri/Iowa) and EQBK carries a much higher NIM (4.36%) with purchase accretion. EQBK's own guide already calls the margin 'modestly lower', so a modest decline is inside the guide; that caps the size. Q2 brokered-deposit share from the EQBK Q2 release https://investor.wedbush.com/wedbush/article/bizwire-2026-7-14-equity-bancshares-inc-second-quarter-results-highlighted-by-strong-earnings-momentum-and-margin-expansion.

findings.finding: The S-4 for the Lincoln Bancorp merger (filed 2026-10-05) puts pre-tax direct merger and issuance costs at $23.7M ($18.8M after tax) against Q2's $0.1M of merger expense; deal signed 2026-09-03 with Hovde as EQBK's adviser, so Q3 GAAP will carry some Lincoln costs (advisory, legal) and GAAP EPS will sit below core, as Q1 2026 GAAP $0.80 did against core $1.32 on Frontier costs. The S-4 also discloses Lincoln NPAs/assets of 3.08% vs a 0.76% peer median and a $27.1M loan fair-value mark; this does not reach Q3 numbers but will be asked about on the call.

What may not be is a GAAP headline below a $1.31 core bar in the wire snapshot (AP's Q2 snapshot quoted GAAP $1.27). Merger costs below operating income with no path to guidance: sized as a fraction.

If the market expected aggressive repurchase the stock would not sit near the Q2 buyback price after a 20-day decline.

findings.finding: The revenue bar sits at the top of the company's own guide: Benzinga's Q3 revenue consensus is about $85.0M, while the guide implies roughly $83-85M (NII ~$74M from 4.25-4.35% NIM on $6.85-6.95B earning assets, plus $9-11M of fees per quarter); Q2 revenue already missed ($81.9M vs $84.9M) while EPS beat on expenses (non-interest expense $46.8M ex merger, down 5.1% q/q). A repeat revenue shortfall with an expense-driven EPS beat is the likeliest shape of the print.

findings.finding: Credit drifted the wrong way in Q2: nonperforming assets rose to $66.3M (0.86% of assets) from $58.4M (0.76%), classified assets 11.9% of regulatory capital, net charge-offs 12bp; the Kansas City Fed's Q2 2026 ag credit survey describes farm finances deteriorating gradually at modest stress (crop producers struggling, cattle strong), relevant to a Kansas/Oklahoma lender with ag exposure. A further NPA rise or a provision above Q2's $1.3M is the downside path for the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced EQBK reaction tied to a credit surprise in the baseline; Q2 NPAs rose and the stock rose 0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Q2 NPA rise is public and was not punished; the ag survey is a regional proxy without a company-level confirmation, so the finding is small. A credit event would show up as a provision well above the ~$2M run-rate the consensus implies.
findings.independence: Proxy: Kansas City Fed ag survey via https://www.nefb.org/news/modest-stress-on-farm-finances (Q2 2026). FB Financial's Q3 NPAs were flat (1.13% vs 1.14%) and net charge-offs 4bp, a different region pointing to benign credit.
